media:group.media:description:
Are you trying to choose between a Tax-Free Savings Account and a Retirement Annuity? Here's what most people get wrong. You don't have to pick just one, you choose what is suitable for your needs and goals.

media:group.media:title: The Two-Pot Retirement System: 3 Things Nobody Is Telling You
media:group.media:description:
Most South Africans are withdrawing from their two-pot savings for the wrong reasons — and it's costing them their future. Here's what you need to know before you touch that money.
South Africa's two-pot retirement system was designed to help households deal with financial shocks — but there are three critical things most people overlook before making a withdrawal. In this video, I break down the system, the tax implications, and the hidden long-term cost of dipping into your savings pot.

entry.title: How to Pay Off Your Home Loan 5 Years Early (R2,000 Extra a Month)

media:group.media:title: How to Pay Off Your Home Loan 5 Years Early (R2,000 Extra a Month)
media:group.media:description:
Imagine finishing off your south african home loan five years early and saving R216,000 in interest! That is the opportunity I have left on the table due to what I can only call pure laziness and not sitting down to do the numbers.12
In this video, I break down the considerations you need to be making when thinking about paying off your home loan sooner. I use my own investment property as an example:
The Property: A two-bedroom apartment in the north of Johannesburg, currently rented out for R9,000 Current Bond Balance: R695,936 Remaining Term: 13 years and 5 months, or 161 months, with a projected payoff date around the year 2039 Current Interest Rate: 9.65% per year, which is below the current prime lending rate of around 10.25% in South Africa.
Current Monthly Payment: R7,790 I show you that if I paid an additional R2,000 every single month (making my total payment R9,790) I would save R216,000 in interest and finish paying off the loan five years earlier, around 2034. If I paid an additional R1,000 (R8,790 total), I would save R110,000 in interest and pay it off three years earlier (around 2036).
Crucial Note: If you pay extra, you must stick with your initial installment (R7,790 in my case) and add the extra amount, even if the bank recalculates and reduces your minimum installment.
Before you jump into paying extra, here are the three major considerations I discuss:
Liquidity: If you are paying extra into an access bond account to save interest, you cannot rely on that same account for emergencies. You need to keep emergency funds somewhere else so that you have liquidity in the event of a financial shock.
Reducing Flexibility: Are you willing to give up the flexibility of spending that extra R2,000 a month on other aspects of your life? If you don't have the money now, consider starting a side hustle that only needs to generate R2,000 extra per month (R500 a week) to ring-fence that money for your loan. Alternative Investment Returns: Where else could you invest that R2,000 to be guaranteed—or at least get—a return above the 9.65% interest rate you are paying on the home loan? This is a math calculation worth thinking about, for example, when deciding whether to contribute to a Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) to reach your R500,000 lifetime limit over the next 13 years. Remember, sometimes it's not just about the numbers; the psychological benefit of wiping away a couple of years of debt is also worth considering.
Disclaimer: None of my videos constitute financial advice. If you are looking for financial advice, please speak to somebody who is certified and registered with the FSCA

entry.title: Stop using your TFSA Like a savings account - 28th FEB is D-DAY

media:group.media:title: Stop using your TFSA Like a savings account - 28th FEB is D-DAY
media:group.media:description:
Most people focus on which provider to choose for a Tax-Free Savings Account.
But that’s the wrong starting point.
A TFSA is not just a savings account. It is a tax wrapper created under the Income Tax Act that allows South Africans to invest up to R36 000 per financial year, with all growth inside that wrapper being tax-free.
And 28 February is the last day to use this year’s allowance.
In this video, we unpack:
• Why a TFSA is a tax rule — not a product • The R36 000 annual limit and the R500 000 lifetime limit • Why cash-based TFSAs may not be the most efficient use of your space • The interest exemption (R23 800 if under 65 | R34 500 if over 65) and why it matters • Why equity investments often make more strategic sense inside the wrapper • Why you should avoid treating your TFSA like an emergency fund • What happens if you withdraw • The 40% penalty for exceeding the annual limit • Why timing your contribution matters • Why fees matter more than most people realise
If you are contributing close to 28 February, remember that clearance times matter. If funds reflect on 1 March, they count toward the new financial year.
A TFSA should be aligned to your long-term goals, not short-term liquidity.
This video is for educational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice. If you need advice specific to your situation, consult a certified financial professional registered with the FSCA.
#TFSA #TaxFreeSavingsAccount #PersonalFinanceSA #Investing101 #FinancialEducation

entry.title: A sit down with Proverb - Reinvention & To Health with It! Book

media:group.media:title: A sit down with Proverb - Reinvention & To Health with It! Book
media:group.media:description:
In this powerful sit-down conversation, ProVerb joins me to unpack failure, reinvention and the lifelong journey toward real health.
From award-winning musician to broadcaster, property investor and now academic, ProVerb reflects on the pivots that shaped his evolution. What looks like diversification from the outside was often driven by necessity, risk awareness and responsibility — especially as a father.
He opens up about: • Squandered opportunities and the “rude awakening” that changed his academic path • Why ego can quietly sabotage financial and personal growth • The discipline of delayed gratification • Letting go of expensive passions that were harming his financial wellness • Building systems instead of relying on hustle • Having open conversations about money with his children • Why health is not a destination — but a continuous journey
His new book, To Health With It, explores a holistic view of health: physical, mental, intellectual, financial, social, occupational and spiritual. In this conversation, he explains why neglecting one dimension inevitably impacts the others — and why true growth requires sacrifice, patience and evolution.
This is not a surface-level celebrity interview. It is a mature conversation about identity, responsibility and becoming.
If you’re navigating reinvention, questioning your career path, or rethinking your relationship with money and health — this one is for you.

entry.title: Financial Foundations: 7 Checks to Build Real Resilience

media:group.media:title: Financial Foundations: 7 Checks to Build Real Resilience
media:group.media:description:
Is your financial plan strong enough to handle change — or does it only work month to month? In this video, we walk through 7 financial checks most people never do to help you reset your finances in 2026 and build a plan that is sustainable, resilient, and aligned to your life goals.
This is not about quick money tips or budgeting hacks. It’s about reviewing the foundations of your personal finances — from cash flow and debt to tax structure, retirement planning, insurance, and estate planning — so your money can actually support your future.
In this video you’ll learn how to:
Check if your cash flow is sustainable, not just surviving month to month
Align your money with short-term and long-term goals using time horizon and risk capacity
Strengthen your risk foundation with emergency funds, income protection, and insurance cover
Improve outcomes through tax efficiency and structure
Reassess debt interest rates, repayment terms, and flexibility
Review retirement planning under the Two-Pot System and understand withdrawal impact
Update estate planning, wills, and beneficiary nominations
Whether you are starting fresh or refining an existing plan, this financial reset checklist for 2026 will help you make smarter, more intentional decisions with your money.

entry.title: The financial triangle you need to build stability, protection and wealth

media:group.media:title: The financial triangle you need to build stability, protection and wealth
media:group.media:description: In this video I introduces the Financial Triangle, a practical framework for managing money in a sustainable order. Using a personal experience of a medical emergency that exposed gaps in my own financial planning, I explains why many people struggle financially despite earning and investing. The video breaks down the four stages of the Financial Triangle: financial survival, risk management, wealth creation, and wealth management, showing why stability and protection must come before investing and legacy planning. The framework helps viewers understand where they are in their financial journey and what to prioritise to avoid financial setbacks.
